claims.text: An API gateway is the single entry point that receives every client request and routes it to the service that answers it, the one place for concerns all requests share, such as TLS and routing.
Defense in depth means stacking independent controls so that one failing or being bypassed does not open the system.

At stage-3 Payments answers GET /api/v1/refunds (staff only) and its Program.cs repeats the API's AddJwtBearer settings: same Authority/MetadataAddress, Audience donhang-api, MapInboundClaims false, RoleClaimType roles.

claims.text: A NetworkPolicy works at the address/port level and never reads a token. Where the CNI plugin enforces policies, a connection from a Pod not allowed is refused before HTTP; traffic from the Pod's own node, e.g. kubelet probes, is always allowed.

claims.text: Checking only at the gateway removes the repeated configuration, but every service then trusts whatever arrives; a route added without the check exposes the service behind it, and a mistake in the shared check exposes all of them.

A gateway pre-check of tokens can be an extra layer only if services keep their own check; Đơn Hàng has not chosen it. For a new staff endpoint in Notifications, add its token check before the HTTPRoute rule and the from-the-gateway entry.
A service cannot rely on how a request reached it: nothing in the request proves it passed a gateway check, so anything reaching the service directly skips a check made only at the gateway.

Any Pod in namespace traefik may connect under from-the-gateway, so a taken-over Pod there with a forged token is stopped by the token check in Payments, since a forged token has no valid Keycloak signature.
